Eleventh Indian Expedition to Antarctica, Scientific Report, 1995 
Department of Ocean Development, Technical Publication No. 9, pp. 1-20 
Prologue to the Aims and Achievements of Eleventh 
Indian Expedition to Antarctica 
S. MUKERJI 
Expedition Leader 
"Ah, but a man's reach 
Should exceed his grasp 
Or what's a heaven for'' 
(R. Browning) 
Introduction 
 Since 1981, when India focussed her attention on Antarctica, It has been a 
story of progress in leaps and bounds. Contributions made by Indian scientists 
within a  short  period  of only a  decade, in  various  disciplines of  Antarctic 
science, are phenomenal. It was with an intention of continuing this process of 
providing valuable inputs to the existing knowledge about Antarctica, that the 
eleventh scientific expedition to this distant land was launched in the austral 
summer of 1991-92. The fury of nature gave rise to an unprecedented situation 
in the context of Indian expeditions, restraining the ship from going alongside 
,ice shelf till as late as 22 February 1992. Yet, almost all the assigned tasks were 
completed. Some of the achievements are the geological investigation of Payer 
and Weyprecht mountains - hitherto a virgin area, recce for future camping sites 
in Conrad and Orvin mountains, GPS observations to set up control points in 
all the ranges of Wohlthat mountain chain from Gruber to Humboldt, systematic 
and detailed study of Antarctic and other birds, studies on Planetary Boundary 
Layer, detailed study.on lichens of Schirmacher Oasi s, large scale topographical 
mapping of the area surrounding Maitri station, etc. Erection of a 28 m tower 
for scientific studies  and  communication purposes,  strengthening of  water 
supply line  and  pumphouse structure, installation of new generators, experi­
ments conducted on HF communication as well as on amateur radio hands and 
record number of flying hours  clocked by  helicopters  despite  bad  weather 
conditions, are highlights from logistic sector. 
2 .
Tasks 
The summer  time  scientific  and  logistic  assignments  for  the  team  are 
outlined below: 
Scientific tasks 
1. Geological investigation of Payer and-Weyprecht mountains in Wohlthat 
range. 
2. Routine  glaciological observations including monitoring of the snout of 
Dakshin Gangotri Glacier in Schumacher Oasis. 
3. Search  for meteorites. 
4. Large  scale topographical mapping of Maitri station area. 
5. GPS  observations in Schinnacher Oasis and Wohlthat mountains for ground 
control points to prepare digital terrain model with the help of SPOT imageries. 
6. Measurement  of aerosol concentration oven Antarctica. 
7. Collection  of data to study the Planetary Boundary Layer (PBL). 
8. Investigation  in  marine  and  fresh  water  eco-systems in  the  Antarctic 
environment. 
9. Studies  on lichenometry in Schirmacher Oasis, Antarctica. 
10. Study  of bacteria in Antarctic soil collected from Schirmacher Oasis. 
11. Investigation  of faunal aspects in Antarctica. 
12. Studies  on  circadian  rhythm  changes  on  human  beings  in  Antarctic 
environment. 
13. Routine  studies in geomagnetism. 
14. Routine  meteorological studies. 
15. Studies  on integrated water vapour content of atmosphere and radio noise 
measurements. 
Logistic tasks 
16. Enhancing  fire protection measures in Maitri station. 
17. Installation  of  new  generator  sets  in  the  genset  accommodation  and 
commissioning of power house. 
18. Improving  the heating system in Maitri station. 
19. Improving  the structure for water supply system at Maitri station. 
20. Erection  of 28 m tower for fixing scientific equipments and communica-
tion antennas. 
21. Routine  maintenance of vehicles. 
22. Erection  of  living and toilet modules in summer camp. 
23. Establishing  data  transfer  facility  using  HF  link  with  India. 
 S  Mukerji

The Voyage 
Expedition ship M.V.THULELAND sailed at 1800  hrs from Mormgao 
harbour, Goa on 27th of November 1991 with 98 members on board. Of these, 
29 were scientists Including 7 member who were to winterover  the  Indian 
station Maitri, drawn from various government organisations, universities and 
national laboratories. Out of the rest, 65 members formed the logistic support 
team with 28 personnel drawn from Indian Army, 18 from Indian Navy and 19 
from Indian Air Force. There was one representative each from Department of 
Ocean Development, Films Division and field of journalism. The team had also 
a meteorologist member from Colombia as guest scientist who was sent by his 
country basically to prepare for a future Colombian expedition to Antarctica. 
The journey was fairly smooth upto the outskirts of Antarctica. Enroute, 
the equator was crossed on 30 November 1991. There was a halt at Port Louis,
